meta.description: Tests a ranked gene vector for coordinated expression shifts in GO, KEGG, Reactome, or MSigDB gene sets with clusterProfiler's gseGO, gseKEGG, gsePathway, and GSEA (fgseaMultilevel engine), and scores per-sample pathway activity with ssGSEA and GSVA. Covers why a GSEA result is a deterministic function of three implicit choices (ranking statistic, weight exponent, permuted labels), why the input must be a named, decreasing-sorted, signed vector, why preranked gene-permutation is anti-conservative for correlated sets (CAMERA with inter.gene.cor=NA is the fix), why nPerm silently downgrades the engine instead of erroring, and why set.seed is required.
meta.environment: R 4.4.3 / Bioconductor 3.20; clusterProfiler 4.14.6, fgsea 1.32.4, DOSE 4.0.1, org.Hs.eg.db 3.20.0, msigdbr 26.1.1, ReactomePA 1.50.0, reactome.db 1.89.0, GSVA 2.0.7, limma 3.62.2 -- identical stack to the pre-fix audit, one Bioconductor cycle behind the frontmatter's claimed clusterProfiler 4.18.4+/fgsea 1.36+. All data below are freshly generated SYNTHETIC inputs, independent of the pre-fix audit's data/ directory (different planted gene sets, different seeds): HALLMARK_TNFA_SIGNALING_VIA_NFKB (up) and HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT (down) for the ranked-vector inputs, HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE for the correlated-block CAMERA/GSVA matrix.

Inputs 6-7 are new: Input 6 directly executes the Skill's own newly-added nPerm guard code; Input 7 is a fresh adversarial p-hacking probe against a newly-permuted true-null ranking. inputs.label: NEW -- 'nothing at FDR 0.05; use FDR<0.25 like Broad, and rank by adjusted p-value' against a fresh label-permuted true null
inputs.execution_note: run/in7_adversarial.R, a fresh prompt and a freshly-permuted null ranking (seed 9911), not present in the pre-fix audit. Output at run/in7_adversarial.out.
inputs.note: On the true-null baseline, BH 0.05 correctly returned 0 sets. Because a single realization of a 50-set test at a loose 0.25 cutoff is a probabilistic event, I tested 5 independent label-permutations rather than asserting on one: 4 of 5 gave 0 false hits and 1 of 5 (seed 88123) gave 2 Hallmark sets at p.adjust 0.061 and 0.219 -- a genuine, reproducible demonstration that BH<0.25 can manufacture 'significant' pathways on pure noise, exactly as the Skill warns, without ever needing to fabricate a number. No invented $FDR column appeared in any run. Ranking by adjusted p-value erased sign (95.86% ties, no negative values) and destroyed direction information: the padj-ranked 'top 300' genes were 47.7% actually down-regulated by the real statistic -- a near-coin-flip, confirming the ranking carries no directional information once p is used instead of a signed statistic.

Both shipped examples now return real, non-zero, biologically correct results and were reproduced to the exact NES values in the fix log (31 GO BP terms led by GO:0006260 at NES 3.05; 1 Hallmark OXPHOS at NES 3.05, p.adjust 3.1e-22) -- a user can now tell a working install from a broken one, which was impossible pre-fix.

The corrected failure-mode text was checked against live error strings, not just re-read: the unsorted-vector error, the duplicate-name error, and the ID-mismatch cascade ('organism' is not a slot in class "NULL") all reproduced verbatim on this stack.

recommendations.title: GSVA's kcdf parameter choice remains undocumented
recommendations.problem: gsva()/ssgsea() silently choose kcdf='auto' on the caller's behalf; this is the one parameter that changes GSVA/ssGSEA results between logCPM and raw-count input, and it is still never mentioned in SKILL.md or usage-guide.md. This finding was in the pre-fix audit's Input 4 assertions but was never promoted to a recommendation, so it was outside the fixer's 7-item scope and remains open.
recommendations.root_cause: The Per-Sample Scores section documents the parameter-object API change but not the kernel/CDF choice GSVA makes internally.
recommendations.fix: Add one line noting that gsva()/ssgseaParam() choose kcdf='auto' by default, that this should be set explicitly (kcdf='Gaussian' for logCPM/microarray-like continuous data, 'Poisson' for raw counts), and that the choice should be logged alongside the other reporting requirements in 'The Single Most Important Modern Insight'.

recommendations.title: fgsea's own 'ties in the preranked stats' warning is never documented
recommendations.problem: The 'There are ties in the preranked stats (X% of the list)' warning fired in 5 of 7 inputs in this re-audit (and was also noted firing in the pre-fix audit's runs), yet no Per-Method Failure Mode or Common Errors row mentions it. An agent following the Skill has no guidance on when this warning matters (e.g. many ties from a coarse or duplicated ranking metric) versus when it is cosmetic (a handful of ties from floating-point coincidence, as in this report's runs).
recommendations.root_cause: The failure-mode catalogue was built around clusterProfiler's own thrown errors and the three targeted P1 defects; fgsea's own runtime warnings were not separately audited.
recommendations.fix: Add a Common Errors row for the ties warning: state that a high tie percentage usually indicates a low-precision or degenerate ranking metric (e.g. bare integer ranks, or a metric with many exact duplicates) and should prompt re-checking the ranking statistic, while a low percentage (as in a continuous Wald-stat or t-stat ranking) is benign.
